title: Make most preventable sudden cardiac deaths predictable and preventable

concept.text: The innovation would be an accessible system that identifies people at actionable risk of sudden cardiac death early enough to offer an intervention proven to improve their survival. It would connect risk assessment, clinical evaluation, treatment selection and delivery, rather than end with a risk score. ECG analysis using machine learning is one possible entry point; the breakthrough requires evidence that acting on the information prevents deaths.

The central target is preventable death from lethal cardiac arrhythmias. Sudden cardiac death involves heterogeneous underlying conditions, and uncertainty in cause-of-death classification complicates identification of arrhythmic deaths. Preventable arrhythmic deaths are therefore a narrower target than all sudden deaths or all cardiac arrests. A predictive marker also does not, by itself, establish who benefits from an implanted defibrillator, medication or another intervention.

Scope proposal: The eventual claim should specify the population being assessed, the time horizon for prediction and prevention, and what counts as a preventable death. These definitions are necessary to make the ambition of preventing “most” such deaths assessable, while preserving the broader goal of reaching people whose risk current clinical practice overlooks.

significance.text: A successful system could turn many first-and-fatal arrhythmic presentations into opportunities for prevention. Implanted cardioverter defibrillators already provide a technical basis for this possibility: they can detect and terminate potentially lethal ventricular arrhythmias. The revolutionary advance would be identifying additional people who benefit from preventive treatment before a fatal event, and reliably getting that treatment to them.

The opportunity extends beyond people with the risk factors usually used to recognize danger. In the 2026 study's Swedish cohort, 41.2% of sudden cardiac deaths occurred among people with none of the specified major risk factors recorded at the time of their ECG: coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction, heart failure, or prior ventricular arrhythmias. This supports the importance of finding overlooked risk, but does not establish that these people had no previously recognized heart disease of any kind.

The impact remains conditional on treatment benefit, population coverage and successful delivery. A high predicted arrhythmic risk does not guarantee that an intervention improves overall survival: competing causes of death can limit the benefit even when sudden cardiac deaths decline. The study notes that some defibrillator trials reduced sudden cardiac death without showing an all-cause mortality benefit. Broad prevention therefore requires more than accurate prediction or a reduction in one classified cause of death.

Conditional downstream possibility: If affordable assessment and effective treatment could be delivered widely, preventive care could reach people outside existing specialist pathways. The scale of that benefit would depend on who receives assessment, who completes follow-up and who can obtain treatment; the supplied evidence does not establish a population-wide effect size.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable identification of treatment-responsive risk. A model must do more than distinguish people who later die from those who do not: its use must identify patients whose outcomes improve when care changes. The 2026 article explicitly calls for a randomized trial because earlier promising predictors have failed to identify patients who benefit from defibrillators. Its observational treatment analysis cannot resolve this causal question.

A related scientific barrier is determining which predicted events are arrhythmic and preventable. Heterogeneous underlying disease, multiple arrhythmic outcomes and imperfect cause-of-death classification make this difficult. A model associated with sudden cardiac death may identify a mixture of mechanisms with different treatment options. The study's focus on younger, healthier high-risk patients reflects the goal of preventing arrhythmic death while limiting the influence of competing mortality.

Engineering and implementation synthesis: A practical system would need dependable performance across patient populations and health systems, accurate absolute-risk estimates over a defined horizon, and a workable response to positive results. Concrete challenges include missed events, false-positive referrals, treatment harms, assessment costs and access to follow-up care. These remain requirements to demonstrate, rather than capabilities established by the supplied study.

current_state.text: Ziad Obermeyer and colleagues' Nature article, “An ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death discovered with deep learning,” was published on 24 June 2026. It reports retrospective risk-model development and validation using ECG data, together with identification of an associated ECG morphology. The model's predictive performance and the interpretable morphology are distinct findings; identifying a morphology does not itself establish a causal mechanism or a treatment target.

In the Swedish held-out evaluation sample, the authors' preferred high-risk group comprised 2.2% of the sample and had a reported annual sudden cardiac death rate of 7.0%. This demonstrates substantial risk enrichment within that selected group. It does not establish that the group contains most future sudden cardiac deaths, that the same absolute risk applies in other populations, or that most preventable deaths can be averted.

The study's defibrillator analysis was observational. Its treatment-associated mortality findings came from patients selected for defibrillators under existing clinical practice, and the authors cautioned that these results were unlikely to generalize to the broader high-risk population. Without randomization, the analysis cannot determine whether defibrillators would lower mortality in patients newly identified by the model. The study did not demonstrate a causal survival benefit from a marker-guided prevention strategy.

The supplied review reports that retained publisher HTML contains the full article text, including Methods. Linked supplementary analyses and original figure images were not inspected, and the main and accompanying PDFs have text-extraction gaps. The earlier account of a failed publisher-page opening and reliance on indexed text cannot be verified from the supplied artifacts. These limitations concern the scope and provenance of the review; they do not establish that the reported scientific results are false. Earlier peer-review results concern an earlier model version and should not replace the final article's findings.

Evidence coverage limitation: The supplied freshness record is empty, so it does not establish whether subsequent work changed the position by 1 November 2026. The dated June result can be described, but the available inputs do not support a comprehensive claim about later developments.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Prospectively validate an affordable assessment strategy across multiple populations and health systems, using a prespecified prediction horizon. Report absolute risks, missed events, false positives and the fraction of subsequent sudden cardiac deaths captured at clinically usable thresholds. Independent replication and transparent reporting should establish reproducibility. Such finite studies would demonstrate performance within the tested settings, without establishing universal applicability.
completion_criteria.label: Affordable risk assessment prospectively validated and independently replicated across populations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal test: Randomized strategy trials should compare assessment linked to a defined treatment pathway with appropriate usual care. They should demonstrate a prespecified, clinically substantial reduction in sudden cardiac death and an improvement in overall mortality, while measuring treatment harms. The intervention must be evaluated in the newly identified patients for whom benefit is being claimed. This proposal addresses the article's explicit call for randomization and its discussion of competing mortality; the exact trial design and success thresholds are not established standards in the supplied source.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized treatment pathways reduce sudden cardiac death and overall mortality

completion_criteria.text: Proposed population-level threshold: A claim to prevent most preventable sudden cardiac deaths should define the target population, prevention horizon and preventable-death denominator in advance, and provide evidence that more than half of those deaths are averted. The denominator must have an explicit method for handling uncertainty in mechanism and preventability. Success in a small high-risk subgroup would support a narrower claim unless population-level evidence establishes the broader effect.
completion_criteria.label: More than half of predefined preventable sudden cardiac deaths averted

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: Demonstrate that assessment, confirmatory evaluation and treatment can be delivered at acceptable cost and with sufficient uptake in the intended health systems. Report where performance or benefit is uncertain, including groups with limited representation or substantial competing mortality. A deployable result should establish the boundaries of its demonstrated benefit as well as its reach.
completion_criteria.label: Pathway delivery achieves acceptable cost and uptake with stated limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CAR-12, “Detect actionable coronary plaque risk before a first clinical event,” shares the aim of identifying actionable danger before an initial event. Its target is coronary plaque risk; CAR-06 targets preventable sudden cardiac death across potentially different underlying conditions and arrhythmic mechanisms. CAR-02, “Reliably reverse advanced atherosclerosis throughout the arterial tree,” could address one underlying disease pathway, but atherosclerosis reversal and arrhythmic risk prediction are distinct capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: CAR-05, “Correct inherited heart disease directly and durably in the beating heart,” could overlap with prevention of sudden death in inherited conditions. It targets durable correction of underlying disease, whereas CAR-06 requires identifying actionable risk and proving the benefit of an appropriate prevention pathway across its defined population. CAR-09, “A durable, non-ablative cure for atrial fibrillation,” also concerns cardiac electrophysiology, but curing atrial fibrillation is distinct from predicting and preventing lethal ventricular arrhythmias.

Roster-based synthesis: CAR-01, “Regenerate a severely damaged adult human heart,” and CAR-08, “Durably reverse heart failure with preserved ejection fraction,” concern recovery from specific forms of cardiac dysfunction. Their populations may overlap with people at risk of sudden death, but restoration of heart function does not by itself demonstrate prediction or prevention of sudden cardiac death. Conversely, CAR-06 could succeed for a defined group without regenerating myocardium or reversing heart failure.

Roster-based synthesis: CAR-03, “A durable, broadly affordable total artificial heart,” CAR-04, “A dependable supply of transplantable animal hearts,” and CAR-07, “Produce a transplantable, fully engineered living human heart,” address replacement of a failing heart. They remain separate from the risk-assessment and prevention pathway proposed here. An implanted defibrillator terminates certain arrhythmias; it does not replace the heart's pumping function.

Roster-based synthesis: CAR-10, “Reverse established calcific aortic stenosis without valve replacement,” CAR-11, “Reverse pulmonary arterial hypertension and its cardiovascular consequences,” and CAR-13, “Broadly prevent cardiac injury from cancer treatment without weakening cancer control,” address particular diseases or sources of injury. Their prevention or treatment could intersect with sudden-death prevention in affected patients, but each requires its own disease-specific evidence. CAR-06 remains a distinct claim about actionable risk identification and demonstrated mortality prevention.

unresolved_issues: The target population, prediction and prevention horizon, and operational definition of a preventable sudden cardiac death remain unspecified.
The supplied evidence does not establish the proportion of future deaths captured by the selected high-risk group or the population fraction avertable through a marker-guided strategy.
Causal treatment benefit, treatment selection and net harms in patients newly identified by the model require randomized evaluation.
Affordability, prospective transportability, delivery capacity and equitable access remain unestablished in the supplied material.
The magnitude that would count as a substantial mortality reduction and the acceptable balance of errors and treatment harms require prespecified operational definitions.
Subsequent developments through 1 November 2026 remain unassessed because no freshness search record was supplied.
Linked supplementary analyses and original figure images were not inspected in the supplied review, and PDF extraction gaps remain. The historical publisher-access failure cannot be verified.

brief.title: Early warning to prevent avoidable sudden heart deaths
possible: People whose danger currently goes unnoticed could learn they face a lethal heart rhythm problem early enough to act. An accessible system would connect that warning to medical evaluation and treatment proven to improve survival.
The goal is to prevent most avoidable deaths from these rhythm problems, including among people current care overlooks.
why: A fatal collapse can be the first sign of danger. Earlier warning would give patients and clinicians a chance to prevent it. Implanted defibrillators, devices that detect and stop dangerous heart rhythms, already offer a way to protect some patients.
Affordable assessment linked to effective care could bring prevention to people outside existing specialist services.

sources.showed: Their model analysed ECGs, recordings of heart electrical activity, and found risk missed by L VEF, a measure of the heart’s pumping function. It also predicted dangerous rhythms in other health systems.
sources.quote: Notably, 86.1% of the model’s high-risk patients were not flagged by L VEF .
sources.cited_for: The study supports using routine heart recordings to find overlooked risk.
sources.not_established: Looking back at patient records does not prove that treating newly flagged people improves survival.

sources.showed: Their computer model distinguished people who later suffered sudden cardiac death from comparison patients using earlier ECGs. It outperformed a conventional ECG risk score.
sources.quote:
The model accurately distinguishes sudden cardiac
death cases from controls, performing better than the conventional ECG
risk score.
sources.cited_for: The study provides another example of heart recordings revealing risk before a collapse.
sources.not_established: Comparing selected cases with controls does not establish reliable population screening or a survival benefit.

sources.showed: Their San Francisco autopsy study found that many presumed sudden cardiac deaths (SCDs) were not arrhythmic, meaning caused by abnormal heart rhythms.
sources.quote: nearly half of presumed SCDs were not arrhythmic.
sources.cited_for: The study shows why identifying the actual cause of sudden death matters for prevention.
sources.not_established: Autopsies clarify causes of death but do not establish which future deaths a screening and treatment system could prevent.

shown: Obermeyer and colleagues identified a group with an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 7% using ECGs. Their model was developed and tested retrospectively, meaning it looked back at existing patient records.

The researchers also found an association between defibrillator use and lower mortality. Patients received devices through existing clinical practice, so this does not establish that devices would save people newly identified by the model.
missing: Affordable assessment has yet to prove reliable in forward-looking studies across populations, with independent teams reproducing the results.
Trials assigning care by chance have yet to show that acting on newly detected risk reduces sudden cardiac deaths and deaths overall.
A complete system has yet to avert most predefined preventable deaths while delivering affordable follow-up and treatment.

milestones.label: Affordable risk assessment proves reliable across populations
milestones.explanation: Studies following patients forward would have to establish affordable prediction across health systems, with independent replication and clear reporting of errors. This would establish where assessment works reliably.

milestones.label: Randomized care trials reduce sudden deaths and overall mortality
milestones.explanation: Trials assigning care by chance would have to show substantial reductions in sudden cardiac deaths and deaths overall among newly identified patients, while measuring harms. This would establish that acting on risk saves lives.

milestones.label: Most predefined preventable sudden cardiac deaths are averted
milestones.explanation: Population studies would have to show that more than half of preventable deaths are averted, using predefined populations, time periods and rules for classifying deaths. This would establish the reach beyond a selected high-risk group.

milestones.label: Affordable care reaches enough people, with clear limits
milestones.explanation: Health systems would have to deliver assessment, evaluation and treatment at acceptable cost, with sufficient participation and clear limits on demonstrated benefit. This would establish whether prevention can reach its intended population.

uncertain: Which population and prediction period should define success, and which deaths should count as preventable?
How many future preventable deaths does the model capture, and which flagged patients would benefit from treatment?
What balance of missed cases, unnecessary treatment and treatment harms would be acceptable?

page.title: Population screening for prevention of sudden cardiac death
page.definition: A programme screens apparently healthy people in a defined population for risk of sudden cardiac death, investigates positive findings and offers treatment shown to reduce such deaths. Sudden cardiac death is an unexpected natural death presumed to have a cardiac cause. In witnessed cases it occurs within one hour of symptom onset, and in unwitnessed cases within 24 hours of the person last being seen alive. An arrhythmic death is caused by an abnormal heart rhythm.

goal.need: In Multnomah County, Oregon, sudden cardiac death occurred at an annual rate of 54 per 100,000 in 2002–2004. Only 121 of 714 cases had a prior measurement of heart function. In 85 of those 121, the left ventricle expelled more than 35% of its blood per beat, above a threshold used to select people for preventive defibrillators. Screening could reach people with unrecognised heart disease in time to prevent a fatal arrest. The benefit of early treatment must outweigh the harms of false alarms, unnecessary tests and treatment.

figures.caption: Autopsy findings in 525 presumed sudden cardiac deaths in San Francisco, from 1 February 2011 to 1 March 2014.
figures.note: Participants were aged 18–90 years and met World Health Organization criteria for sudden cardiac death before autopsy. Arrhythmic classification does not itself establish preventability.

statements.quote: How to identify high-risk patients in low-risk groups and low-risk patients in high-risk groups remains a fundamental challenge.

statements.body: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Sudden Cardiac Death Prevention Working Group
statements.quote: scalable sensors/monitoring devices that can be used to identify risk factors and triggers of sudden cardiac death and sudden cardiac arrest.
statements.context: Recommendation 5 calls for developing and validating these devices; the recommendation is reproduced in National Academies workshop proceedings.

statements.body: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute working group on screening for sudden cardiac death in the young
statements.quote: whether screening for SCDY would effectively reduce SCD and add overall healthcare value
statements.context: The working group was charged with evaluating screening for sudden cardiac death in the young. It defined value as improved clinical outcomes at an acceptable cost-benefit ratio.

completion.title: Population screening linked to treatment reduces sudden cardiac mortality with benefits exceeding harms.
completion.criterion: Meet the mortality branch of UK NSC criterion 11: high-quality randomized controlled trials establish that the complete screening-to-treatment programme reduces sudden cardiac mortality in its intended population compared with no organized screening. Criterion 13 additionally requires benefits to outweigh harms, including overtreatment, false positives, false reassurance and complications. The committee specifies no minimum percentage reduction or fixed follow-up period.
completion.set_by: UK National Screening Committee, general population-screening appraisal criteria 11 and 13; the mortality branch is applied here to sudden cardiac death.
completion.threshold_quote: There should be evidence from high quality randomised controlled trials that the screening programme is effective in reducing mortality or morbidity.
completion.basis: The UK National Screening Committee assesses the complete programme, including treatment and harms. Its recommendation against systematic screening under age 39 applies to that age group. In a subsequent UK cohort, all 104,369 participants aged 14–35 underwent screening. Follow-up identified 15 survived cardiac arrests and 20 sudden cardiac deaths. Without an unscreened comparison group, those counts cannot establish how many deaths screening prevented.

milestones.title: A marker measured before an event is associated with sudden cardiac death or a condition that causes it.
milestones.criterion: Establish robust evidence that a marker measurable before cardiac arrest is associated with subsequent sudden cardiac death or with a serious or treatable cardiac condition that can cause it.
milestones.set_by: UK National Screening Committee, criterion 1, reproduced in its 2019 SCD review of ages 12–39. That review did not assess the marker–disease component of the criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: robust evidence about the association between the risk or disease marker and serious or treatable disease

milestones.title: A sudden cardiac death screening test is validated for its target population with an agreed cutoff.
milestones.criterion: Validate a simple, safe and precise screening test for the intended population. Establish the distribution of test values in that population and define and agree a suitable cutoff for a positive result.
milestones.set_by: UK National Screening Committee, general criteria 4–5. Criterion 4 was also applied to SCD screening at ages 12–39 in the 2019 review.
milestones.threshold_quote: a suitable cut-off level defined and agreed.

milestones.title: Presymptomatic treatment improves outcomes for people identified by screening compared with usual care.
milestones.criterion: For people in whom screening identifies a condition associated with sudden cardiac death, show that treatment before symptoms appear leads to better outcomes for the screened individual than usual care.
milestones.set_by: UK National Screening Committee, general criterion 9 and the treatment requirement on its SCD recommendation page.
milestones.threshold_quote: intervention at a pre-symptomatic phase leads to better outcomes for the screened individual compared with usual care.

milestones.title: An agreed policy specifies diagnostic follow-up and patient choices after a positive screen.
milestones.criterion: Agree which further diagnostic investigations to offer people who screen positive for risk of sudden cardiac death and what choices are available to them.
milestones.set_by: UK National Screening Committee, population screening criterion 7.
milestones.threshold_quote: an agreed policy on the further diagnostic investigation of individuals with a positive test result and on the choices available to those individuals.

not_found: No numerical population-wide target for averting most preventable sudden cardiac deaths was found in searches of NHLBI/HRS recommendations, ESC guidance, UK NSC criteria and registered trial endpoints.
No randomised comparison of population screening with usual care was identified that demonstrated fewer sudden cardiac deaths and a net benefit.

results.finding: Among 35,417 Swedish patients, ECG model high-risk recordings had a 7.0% annual sudden cardiac death rate.
results.detail: The ECG preceded the outcome. The model was also evaluated in external US and Taiwanese datasets.
results.quote:
Our preferred high-risk group comprises 2.2% of the sample, and has 
an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 7.0% (95% CI: 4.9–9.5%; survival 
analysis in Supplementary Information section I.C).

results.finding: Among 35,417 Swedish patients, the selected ECG high-risk group had a 7.0% annual sudden cardiac death rate.
results.detail: The retrospective study selected a threshold and evaluated risk in patients with recorded ECGs. It did not validate a screening test with an agreed cutoff in an asymptomatic target population.
results.quote:
Our preferred high-risk group comprises 2.2% of the sample, and has 
an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 7.0% (95% CI: 4.9–9.5%; survival 
analysis in Supplementary Information section I.C).

results.finding: In a regression using 119,541 ECGs, high-risk patients with defibrillators had 54.4% lower sudden cardiac mortality than predicted.
results.detail: This observational comparison is vulnerable to confounding. Patients were selected for defibrillators under existing practice; the study did not establish that treatment of newly screen-detected risk improves outcomes versus usual care.
results.quote:
In absolute terms, high-risk patients with defibrilla-
tors die 3.62 percentage points (p.p.) less than their predicted rate of 
6.65 p.p., a reduction of 54.4% (P < 0.001; the predicted rate sums the 
baseline rate in the low-risk population; that is, intercept plus age and 
sex effects at population means, with the high-risk indicator and the 
defibrillator indicator.)

results.finding: The pre-event ECG score had an AUC of 0.872 for one-year sudden cardiac death in 113,072 ECGs from 35,417 Swedish patients.
results.detail: The Swedish death-certificate definition can include non-arrhythmic deaths. The external cohorts tested ventricular arrhythmias and arrhythmic arrests as distinct endpoints.
results.quote:
We calculate discrimination using the area under the receiver-  
operating-characteristic curve (AUC): 0.872 (patient-level boot -
strapped 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.843–0.899).

results.finding: In 113,072 ECGs from 35,417 Swedish patients, the proposed positive cutoff identified a group with 7.0% one-year sudden cardiac mortality.
results.detail: The authors anchored their cutoff to mortality in defibrillator trial control groups. Applying the same absolute cutoff in the US flagged 3.4% of ECGs, and the US endpoint was ventricular arrhythmia.
results.quote:
Our preferred high-risk group comprises 2.2% of the sample, and has 
an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 7.0% (95% CI: 4.9–9.5%; survival 
analysis in Supplementary Information section I.C).

results.finding: In a Swedish analysis of 119,541 ECGs from 35,885 patients, high-risk defibrillator recipients had 54.4% lower sudden cardiac mortality than predicted.
results.detail: Patients received defibrillators under existing clinical practice. The comparison uses a regression expectation, and unmeasured confounding could explain some or all of the association.
results.quote:
High-risk ECG patients with defibrillators implanted were 54.4% less likely to die than 
expected, suggesting a mortality benefit.

results.finding: A pre-arrest ECG score distinguished later cardiac arrest cases from controls in external validation (n=1,043, AUROC 0.820).
results.detail: The study's case definition included successfully resuscitated arrests. Cases also needed an archived pre-arrest ECG, which may have favored people with prior cardiac evaluation.
results.quote:
In the external validation dataset, the DL model achieved a comparable
AUROC of 0.820 (0.794–0.847) in detecting SCD cases.

results.finding: The resting ECG model achieved 79.6% specificity at the study threshold in external case-control validation (n=1,043).
results.detail: The model was limited to sinus rhythm ECGs. Controls were selected to have a high prevalence of coronary artery disease, and the case-control design precluded reliable estimates of positive and negative predictive values.
results.quote:
The sensitivity was
0.763 (0.733–0.796), while the speciﬁcity was 0.796 (0.753–0.838).

results.finding: Among 525 presumed sudden cardiac deaths, 37% of autopsy-defined arrhythmic deaths had prior dyslipidemia.
results.detail: Premortem histories came from available clinical records. The study had no standardized baseline measurements or living comparison group.
results.quote: History of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and congestive heart failure (CHF) was more common in autopsy-defined SADs

results.finding: In ARIC (n=15,792), a high baseline ECG risk score was associated with an adjusted hazard ratio of 4.84 for subsequent sudden cardiac death.
In ARIC (n=15,792), 1.1% of participants reached the candidate high-risk ECG threshold at baseline.
results.detail: The analysis excluded ECGs with rhythms or conduction patterns that prevented scoring, which limits what it establishes about test performance across a screening population.
results.quote: Only 1.1% of ARIC participants presented with ≥4 ECG abnormalities at the baseline visit

results.finding: In 11,168 adolescent soccer players, each ECG rule detected 86% of those with serious cardiac pathology.
results.detail: The reported detection rate pools serious cardiac diagnoses, so it cannot establish the association for a specific condition that can cause sudden cardiac death.
results.quote: All four criteria identified 36 (86%) of 42 athletes with serious cardiac pathology.

results.finding: In 11,168 British adolescent soccer players, the 2017 ECG recommendations had 86% sensitivity for serious cardiac pathology.
results.detail: The study retrospectively compared four published interpretation rules. The international rules classified 3.6% of black players and 1.6% of white players as abnormal.
results.quote: The international recommendations demonstrated the highest specificity for white (99%) and black (97%) athletes and a sensitivity of 86%.

results.finding: Among 3,620 high school athletes screened, 15 of 16 diagnosed with a condition associated with sudden cardiac death had an abnormal ECG.
results.detail: The 15 of 16 figure counts any abnormal ECG. The study excluded abnormalities deemed unrelated to the final diagnosis when calculating sensitivity.
results.quote: The ECG was flagged as abnormal in 15 of 16 (93.8%) cases.

results.finding: Among 3,620 high school athletes, resting ECG had 87.5% sensitivity for conditions associated with sudden cardiac death.
results.detail: Clinicians read ECGs alongside the history and examination. Athletes with fully negative screens did not receive echocardiography, so the study may have missed structural disease.
results.quote: The sensitivity (18.8%), specificity (68.0%), and positive predictive value (0.3%) of the AHA 14‐point evaluation was substantially lower than the sensitivity (87.5%), specificity (97.5%), and positive predictive value (13.6%) of ECG.

results.finding: Among 104,369 young people screened, ECG sensitivity for detecting conditions associated with sudden cardiac arrest or death was 75.4%.
results.detail: Cardiologists recommended secondary evaluation when appropriate. The text does not report systematic diagnostic verification across ECG-positive and ECG-negative participants.
results.quote: The sensitivity of the ECG and the questionnaire for detecting conditions associated with SCA/SCD was 75.4% and 32.5%, respectively.

results.finding: Among 104,369 young people screened once, 280 had a condition associated with sudden cardiac arrest or death.
results.detail: The source is a charity webpage reproducing the abstract of a peer-reviewed JACC paper.
results.quote: Screening identified 280 (0.3%) individuals with conditions associated with SCA/SCD, of whom 115 (41%) received risk-modifying interventions, including 10 prophylactic implantable cardioverter defibrillators and 2 cardiac transplants.

results.finding: Among 4,655 Kagoshima seventh graders, the proposed Fridericia-corrected QT screening cutoff was 445 ms.
results.detail: The authors report that the proposed cutoffs had yet to be applied in Japan’s school screening programme or checked against genetically or clinically diagnosed long QT syndrome.
results.quote:
The tentative cut-offs 
suitable for screening subjects with prolonged QT intervals 
are 430 ms for 1st graders, 445 ms for 7th graders, and 440 
and 455 ms for 10th grade boys and girls, respectively.

results.finding: Among 10,282 one-month-old infants in Japan, ECG screening identified a Bazett-corrected QT cutoff of ≥450 ms for persistent QT prolongation.
results.detail: Repeat ECGs were triggered by an initial QTc of ≥450 ms, so persistent prolongation below that threshold could have been missed and the reported sensitivity may be inflated.
results.quote: Statistical analysis showed that a cutoff QTc(B) ≥0.45 was optimal for screening infants with a pQTc.

results.finding: Among 44,596 apparently healthy Italian neonates screened by ECG, mean QTc was 406 ms.
results.detail: Genotyping was selective and incomplete, leaving sensitivity undetermined. The threshold for repeat ECG differed from the threshold for genetic testing, which was broadened during the study.
results.quote: Mean heart rate was 153±16 b/min, mean QT interval was 256±18 ms, mean QTc was 406±20 ms and slightly longer in females than in males (407±20 and 405±20 ms, p<0.001).

results.finding: Japanese school screening guidelines specify 12-lead ECG and specialist examination after referral to secondary screening (policy recommendation, sample size not applicable).
results.detail: The 48% figure describes local practice. The guideline leaves additional testing to clinical judgment based on symptoms and screening findings.
results.quote: The secondary heart disease screening should consist of a 12-lead ECG and examination by an expert.

results.finding: For asymptomatic youth with a Wolff–Parkinson–White ECG pattern, all 13 writing committee members approved a pathway specifying follow-up tests and patient choices.
results.detail: The pathway applies to screen-detected ventricular preexcitation as well as incidental findings. Patients, parents, and clinicians jointly make the individual care plan.
results.quote:
All writing
members approved the ﬁnal version.

definition = "A programme screens apparently healthy people in a defined population for risk of sudden cardiac death, investigates positive findings and offers treatment shown to reduce such deaths. Sudden cardiac death is an unexpected natural death presumed to have a cardiac cause. In witnessed cases it occurs within one hour of symptom onset, and in unwitnessed cases within 24 hours of the person last being seen alive. An arrhythmic death is caused by an abnormal heart rhythm.". Reason: The definition omits the witnessed and unwitnessed time windows that distinguish the mortality endpoint used in population studies.

goal.need = "In Multnomah County, Oregon, sudden cardiac death occurred at an annual rate of 54 per 100,000 in 2002\u20132004. Only 121 of 714 cases had a prior measurement of heart function. In 85 of those 121, the left ventricle expelled more than 35% of its blood per beat, above a threshold used to select people for preventive defibrillators. Screening could reach people with unrecognised heart disease in time to prevent a fatal arrest. The benefit of early treatment must outweigh the harms of false alarms, unnecessary tests and treatment.". Reason: The 70% figure applies to cases with a prior measurement, and the current text omits both the potential benefit of earlier treatment and the harms of false positives.

add statement by National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute working group on screening for sudden cardiac death in the young, 2011: "whether screening for SCDY would effectively reduce SCD and add overall healthcare value". Reason: The working group explicitly asked whether screening prevents deaths in young people, a question the existing statements about risk prediction leave open.

edit completion: basis = "The UK National Screening Committee assesses the complete programme, including treatment and harms. Its recommendation against systematic screening under age 39 applies to that age group. In a subsequent UK cohort, all 104,369 participants aged 14\u201335 underwent screening. Follow-up identified 15 survived cardiac arrests and 20 sudden cardiac deaths. Without an unscreened comparison group, those counts cannot establish how many deaths screening prevented."; refs = [5, 6, 13]. Reason: The basis omits a large cohort that illustrates why finding and treating disease cannot by itself establish a reduction in sudden cardiac mortality.

edit m1: title = "A marker measured before an event is associated with sudden cardiac death or a condition that causes it."; criterion = "Establish robust evidence that a marker measurable before cardiac arrest is associated with subsequent sudden cardiac death or with a serious or treatable cardiac condition that can cause it."; threshold_quote = "robust evidence about the association between the risk or disease marker and serious or treatable disease"; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7, 5, 1, 17]. Reason: The criterion mixes the marker-association test with results from a case–control study whose cases included survivors of arrest.

edit m2: criterion = "Validate a simple, safe and precise screening test for the intended population. Establish the distribution of test values in that population and define and agree a suitable cutoff for a positive result."; threshold_quote = "a suitable cut-off level defined and agreed."; threshold_ref = 5; refs = [5, 7]. Reason: The Swedish study’s selected fraction of recordings and observed event rate appear inside the criterion even though the committee requires a cutoff agreed for the intended population.

add milestone after m2: "An agreed policy specifies diagnostic follow-up and patient choices after a positive screen.". Reason: The current sequence jumps from a positive screening result to treatment without the committee’s required policy for diagnostic investigation and patient choices.

edit m3: title = "Presymptomatic treatment improves outcomes for people identified by screening compared with usual care."; criterion = "For people in whom screening identifies a condition associated with sudden cardiac death, show that treatment before symptoms appear leads to better outcomes for the screened individual than usual care."; threshold_quote = "intervention at a pre-symptomatic phase leads to better outcomes for the screened individual compared with usual care."; threshold_ref = 5; refs = [5, 6]. Reason: The defibrillator trial enrolled patients after myocardial infarction, whereas this milestone concerns the benefit of treating people identified through screening before symptoms.
